items.prompt:
When a text deliberately leaves its meaning open, it is:
A) ambiguous
B) a summary
C) a title

'Strong' textual evidence is the:
A) most convincing evidence
B) longest sentence
C) first word

An inference is a conclusion drawn from:
A) evidence and reasoning
B) a guess
C) the title

Read.

She thanked them 'for everything,' though her clenched jaw and the slammed door told another story.

The strongest evidence shows she is actually:
A) grateful
B) angry
C) bored

steps: Jaw + slammed door. Key is B.

items.prompt:
A story ends with a soldier staring at an open gate, and we never learn if he walks through. The author has:
A) deliberately left the outcome uncertain
B) made an error
C) resolved the plot fully
items.answer: A) deliberately left the outcome uncertain

solution.answer: A) deliberately left the outcome uncertain

items.prompt:
'Strong AND thorough' evidence means it is:
A) the most convincing, and there is enough of it
B) a single weak detail
C) unrelated to the claim
items.answer: A) the most convincing, and there is enough of it

solution.answer: A) the most convincing, and there is enough of it

items.prompt:
Why might an author deliberately leave a key matter UNCERTAIN at a story's end?
A) to invite interpretation and reflect life's real complexity
B) because they forgot to finish
C) to avoid having any meaning
items.answer: A) to invite interpretation and reflect life's real complexity

solution.answer: A) to invite interpretation and reflect life's real complexity

items.prompt:
Which is the WEAKEST evidence that a character feels guilty?
A) 'He couldn't sleep and avoided the victim's family.'
B) 'He owns a gray coat.'
C) 'He flinched whenever the subject came up.'

steps: Irrelevant to guilt. Key is B.
